newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Minyuan suspended on investigation.
newsitem.headline: China Minyuan suspended on investigation.

text.p: China has ordered the suspension of trading in shares in the Shenzhen-listed A share firm Hainan Minyuan Modern Agriculture Development Co on alleged violation of accounting rules, local media said on Wednesday.

The Shenzhen stock exchange suspended trading in Minyuan on February 28 pending an investigation into suspected violation of the rules by the firm in its 1996 annual report issued last month, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said.
"There have been a lot of complaints from investors since the publication of Minyuan's annual report," the newspaper said.
"To maintain order and protect investors, authorities are investigating the company," it said.
The newspaper gave no further details and company officials reached by telephone declined to comment.
China has been tightening supervision of the stock markets since late last year.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), the country's top securities watchdog, issued new rules on Tuesday banning those found to have engaged in insider trading or price manipulation from the industry permanently or at least for a few years.

Minyuan, a Hainan-based producer of agricultural and acquatic products which has been diversifying into property, tourism and telecommunications, said in its 1996 annual report that it had chalked up a 1996 net profit of 485.29 million yuan against the previous year's 375,704 yuan.
Net earnings per share hit 0.867 yuan versus 0.0009 yuan in 1995, while turnover reached 16.78 million yuan against 3.64 million yuan in 1995, the report said.
The report said the earnings came largely from the sale and rental of its 70.83 percent-owned 40,000-square-metre Minyuan Building, an office complex in Beijing completed last June.
The report said the firm planned to conduct a 9.8-for-10 bonus issue for all shareholders from its 1996 earnings. The firm last year had offered a three-for-10 bonus issue from its 1995 earnings.
"Its 1996 profit was unbelievable," a broker said.

Before its suspension, Minyuan's A shares were at 23.49 yuan per share, compared with 2.01 yuan in April last year when China's stock markets began to surge on the back of an improving national economy.
Minyuan is the second listed firm to be suspended from trading on allegations of accounting-related rule violations in the six-year history of modern China's stock markets.
In August last year, Shanghai-listed Shandong Bohai Group Co was suspended on the same allegations.
Shangdong Bohai was later found guilty of issuing incorrect information that contravened China's accounting regulations. The company was punished by the securities watchdog, CSRC.
